react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of 12 differentially abundant metabolites identified Tryptophan metabolism as the overwhelming biological winner, achieving unanimous consensus across three independent analytical methods: RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 8.59e-19), Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p=0.0024), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA (p=5.41e-09). Seven tryptophan-axis metabolites drove this signal — L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), serotonin (C00780), quinolinic acid (C03722), and melatonin (C01598) — collectively mapping across the kynurenine branch (3-HANA, quinolinic acid → NAD+ biosynthesis), the serotonin/melatonin branch (tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin), and the decarboxylation branch (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde). This multi-branch perturbation implicates systemic dysregulation of tryptophan allocation, with potential consequences for neuroimmune signaling (serotonin depletion) and NAD+ homeostasis (kynurenine overload). Five input metabolites (deoxyribose 1-phosphate, 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1, N-formyl-L-glutamic acid, acetylcholine, dihydrolipoate) were not captured by tryptophan pathways in any paradigm, suggesting they belong to independent biological processes (pentose phosphate, xenobiotic metabolism, folate, cholinergic, and mitochondrial redox pathways).

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment analysis identified Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 at rank 0 with FDR = 8.59e-19, hitting 7 of the 12 input metabolites (L-tryptophan, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, serotonin, quinolinic acid, melatonin). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA returned the equivalent KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with p = 5.41e-09, hitting 6 metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 with p = 0.0021, hitting 8 metabolites. WikiPathways confirmed the same signal in WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism, FDR = 4.02e-15) and WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR = 9.41e-11). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 2.14e-08) was also significant. The Kynurenine branch of tryptophan metabolism is supported by 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) membership. The serotonin/melatonin branch is supported by L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), and melatonin (KEGG:C01598) membership. The decarboxylation branch is supported by tryptamine (KEGG:C00398) and indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) membership. Five additional metabolites (deoxyribose 1-phosphate, 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1, N-formyl-L-glutamic acid, acetylcholine, dihydrolipoate) were captured by mummichog in secondary pathways (pentose phosphate pathway, glycerophospholipid metabolism, vitamin B9/folate metabolism, ascorbate metabolism) but did not achieve pathway-level significance across ORA tools.

  "narrative_text": "Cross-paradigm enrichment analysis identified Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 at rank 0 with FDR = 8.59e-19, hitting 7 of the 12 input metabolites (L-tryptophan, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, serotonin, quinolinic acid, melatonin). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA returned the equivalent KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with p = 5.41e-09, hitting 6 metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 with p = 0.0021, hitting 8 metabolites. WikiPathways confirmed the same signal in WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism, FDR = 4.02e-15) and WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR = 9.41e-11). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 2.14e-08) was also significant. The Kynurenine branch of tryptophan metabolism is supported by 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) membership. The serotonin/melatonin branch is supported by L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), and melatonin (KEGG:C01598) membership. The decarboxylation branch is supported by tryptamine (KEGG:C00398) and indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) membership. Five additional metabolites (deoxyribose 1-phosphate, 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1, N-formyl-L-glutamic acid, acetylcholine, dihydrolipoate) were captured by mummichog in secondary pathways (pentose phosphate pathway, glycerophospholipid metabolism, vitamin B9/folate metabolism, ascorbate metabolism) but did not achieve pathway-level significance across ORA tools.",

MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA returned the equivalent KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with p = 5.41e-09, hitting 6 metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 with p = 0.0021, hitting 8 metabolites. WikiPathways confirmed the same signal in WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism, FDR = 4.02e-15) and WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR = 9.41e-11). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 2.14e-08) was also significant. The Kynurenine branch of tryptophan metabolism is supported by 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) membership.
